plugins.name: guard
plugins.description: Nothing is audited until you ask for it. `/guard:audit-turn` runs guard's router subagent over the answer the finished turn wrote, and the router names which audit agents would actually find something in it — unsupported claims, deferrals the repo could answer, explanation the reader cannot follow, unnatural Korean, comments in the source it edited, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md that drifted from a map into a payload, saved reference docs that filled up with local reasoning — each with a reason; they run together and nothing is corrected until all of them have reported, so every audit judges the same text — then the ones that found something read the corrections once more. `/guard:audit-report <path>` does the same for a standalone document. When a turn ends guard recommends nothing: it records the turn verbatim and names the file the answer was written to, which is what makes an audit asked for an hour later able to correct the document the user actually has — and it is that file, translated for a reader who does not read English, that the turn is delivered from. A documentation agent reports where a cited document is — already saved, in the repository, or in a knowledge base the project configures — and fetches and saves the primary source when only the network has it; a saved reference the turn wrote is checked by an auditor of its own. One switch per agent, all off until you turn one on, plus two saved settings for whether a session starts armed: the plan gate armed unless the project says otherwise, the turn side muted until you arm it, since every turn pays for the answer file even though no audit runs unasked; `guard on` / `guard off` move just the session you are in. A `handover` skill writes a self-contained session handover before you clear the conversation, and the session `/clear` opens next is offered it: guard carries the file's path across that boundary and the session asks whether to read it. Claude Code and Codex. Requires Python 3.11+.

plugins.name: peers
plugins.description: A peer is a Claude Code session running somewhere else on this machine — another repository, another checkout, another project. This plugin finds the peer already serving a folder and reuses the context it has built up, or starts one there and tells you which folder is getting an agent before it does; the peer runs under that project's own permission settings, never a mode the plugin imposed. Tasks go out with a reply address written into them, because a peer's answer reaches you only if the peer sends it, and you are told when one finishes instead of waiting on it. Two peers can also be introduced to each other to settle a cross-repository question directly, with one of them named as the reporter. Background peers it started can be stopped when the work is done; a session you started yourself in a terminal is left to you. Claude Code only — Codex has no cross-session messaging. Requires the `claude` CLI and `uv`.
